newsitem.title: ITALY: ITALY JULY CAR ORDERS SEEN UP, FUTURE STABLE -CSP.
newsitem.headline: ITALY JULY CAR ORDERS SEEN UP, FUTURE STABLE -CSP.

text.p: Italian orders for new cars showed a moderate increase in July over June and expectations for the next quarter see deliveries holding steady, car sector research body Centro Studi Promotor (CSP) said.

CSP said in its latest monthly report that the volume of orders, following a slowdown immediately after an initial surge when the government's car buying incentive scheme was introduced in January, showed a modest recovery in July.
In its regular survey of car dealers, CSP said the number seeing high levels of orders had increased over June and it also showed that half the new cars ordered benefited from the incentive scheme.
Some 55 percent of dealers polled saw deliveries remaining steady over the next three to four months.
CSP noted the government's decision to extend to incentive scheme until next July from its originally planned end in September would aid the continued recovery of the domestic market.

Transport Ministry figures on Friday showed Italian new car registrations rose 54.06 percent year-on-year in July to 246,500 units. In the seven-month period January to July this year, new car registrations rose 34.4 percent to 1,558,900 vehicles.
